header.title: Learning Analytics for Interdisciplinary Project-based Learning (LAIP)
header.subtitle:
Learning Analytics for Interdisciplinary Project-based Learning:
Bridging Paradigms

faq.question: What is LAIP?
faq.answer: LAIP (Learning Analytics for Interdisciplinary Project-based Learning) is a half-day interactive LAK27 workshop. It focuses on how learning analytics can support interdisciplinary project-based learning (iPBL), and brings together researchers from multimodal, social, contextual, and AI-supported learning analytics. It builds on the outcomes of the TELIP workshop at EC-TEL 2026.

faq.question: What is the aim of this workshop?
faq.answer: This workshop aims to initiate a conversation on conceptual and analytical framing for iPBL by bridging learning analytics paradigms, and to create an initial map linking learning challenges, data, measurement, and intervention opportunities in iPBL.

faq.question: What happens during the workshop?
faq.answer: The workshop has five parts: an introduction establishing common ground on iPBL; brief presentations of selected abstract contributions; group work mapping learning analytics approaches to iPBL challenges; synthesis of group results in plenary; and closing with an agreed agenda for follow-up steps.

faq.question: Who should attend?
faq.answer: Researchers from learning analytics communities (e.g., multimodal, social, contextual and workplace, and AI-supported learning analytics) working on or interested in complex, longitudinal, collaborative learning settings such as iPBL.

survey.title: Share your perspective before we meet
survey.text: Participate in a 20-minute survey that challenges you to reflect on the conceptual and analytical challenges of iPBL. You can also submit an optional extended abstract that (a) takes a perspective on iPBL, related concepts and challenges, (b) connects completed or ongoing work to these challenges, and (c) clarifies the data involved. Your input grounds the group work during the workshop.

description.title: Motivation
paragraphs: Interdisciplinary project-based learning (iPBL), in which students from multiple disciplines work together on extended projects, poses a distinct challenge for learning analytics (LA). Learning unfolds over weeks across changing project phases, individual and team processes, and fragmented multimodal traces, including digital traces, conversations, and evolving project artifacts. While existing LA approaches address parts of this challenge, they seldom integrate longitudinal digital traces, team interactions, and project artifacts to track learning across phases and inform timely support for students, teams, and educators.

One possible reason for this gap is that iPBL sits at the intersection of learning analytics paradigms. An existentialist perspective can help capture the situated and participant-dependent nature of learning in open-ended interdisciplinary projects, while an ontological perspective can help connect individual activity, team interaction, project phases, and outcomes as parts of an evolving system. This workshop bridges these paradigms by bringing together learning analytics perspectives that study rich, situated interaction with approaches that trace learning longitudinally across project phases and digital environments. By connecting analytics to actionable support for learners, teams, and educators, the workshop aligns with LAK27's focus on helping individuals and communities thrive.

goals.title: Workshop goals
goals.intro: Building on the outcomes of the TELIP workshop at EC-TEL 2026, this workshop shifts the focus to integrating different learning analytics paradigms. Our goal is to initiate a conversation on conceptual and analytical framing for iPBL and to bring together scholars from different LAK communities. Specifically, the workshop pursues the following objectives:
exampleQuestions: Elaborate on the conceptual underpinnings and practical challenges of iPBL identified in the TELIP workshop.
Create an initial map connecting iPBL learning challenges with relevant data sources, learning analytics approaches, measures, and opportunities for intervention.
Develop an outline for a conceptual paper mapping learning analytics approaches for iPBL.
Connect communities working across learning analytics paradigms and explore the formation of a special interest group (SIG) on iPBL.

participation.title: Participation & format
participation.intro: To participate in the half-day session, complete the {{surveyLink}} and, optionally, submit an extended abstract through the survey. Make sure you register for the 17th International Conference on Learning Analytics & Knowledge (LAK27). Places are limited (about 25 participants). Two members of the organizing team will review submitted abstracts based on their relevance to iPBL challenges, clarity about the data and analytic approach involved, and potential to connect different learning analytics paradigms. Up to five abstracts will be selected for presentation.
participation.formatIntro: The workshop runs as an interactive half-day event (3.5 hours) and is organized in five parts:
formatSteps: Introduction (30 min): Establishing common ground on iPBL with a common definition, a summary of the results from the TELIP workshop (conceptual framing, context in cases, challenges, and research areas), and results of the pre-workshop survey.

Abstract presentations (45 min): Brief presentations of selected abstract contributions in a common structure (challenge addressed, data involved, analytic approach, open questions), followed by guided discussion that relates these inputs to one another.
Group work (90 min): Small groups extend the identified challenges, map LA approaches from related paradigms and communities to these challenges, and formulate methodological research questions.
Synthesis (30 min): Groups present their results in plenary and negotiate how to integrate them into a joint outcome.
Closing (15 min): Agreement on an agenda for follow-up steps.

outcomes.title: Expected outcomes
outcomes.intro: By bringing together researchers from different LAK communities, the workshop seeks to connect perspectives across modalities, levels of analysis, and project phases, and to give learning analytics a stronger methodological foundation for studying the complex, longitudinal, and socially distributed learning processes that iPBL is designed to foster. Participants will help create an initial framework for studying complex, longitudinal, collaborative learning settings.

items.title: Integrated map of analytics for iPBL
items.text: An integrated map linking learning challenges, data, measurement, and intervention opportunities in iPBL, developed in group work and plenary synthesis.

items.title: Methodological research agenda
items.text: Methodological research questions formulated in subgroups and integrated into an agreed research agenda for learning analytics in iPBL.

items.title: Community-authored synthesis
items.text: An outline for a community-authored conceptual paper mapping analytics for iPBL, and a report synthesizing the agreed research agenda for those who decide to contribute.

items.title: Lasting collaboration
items.text: Integration of communities working across learning analytics paradigms through the formation of a special interest group (SIG) on iPBL and a possible follow-up workshop.
